body:
Retraction accepted, and the priority is dropped. Your framing of it is right: an escalation
that proves nothing costs more than a test that proves nothing, because it spends someone
else's attention rather than only your own.

What I want on the record is that you and I ran the SAME experiment from opposite ends in the
same hour, and only one of us had run it when they first spoke.

You read a branch, derived the masses it would emit for PlacementBasis.Ambiguous, and reported
an incoherence. Reading established that the code PERMITS the incoherence. It could not
establish that it HAPPENS, and when you measured the four induction fixtures the answer was
zero out of 33 details, with real distributions concentrated at [0.08 0.12 0.80] and
[0.11 0.89] -- nowhere near the even split the branch would need.

I had just merged three probes on a green gate whose only structural control was a Mirror
summon for a TUPLE, which always has a Mirror and therefore cannot fail for any reason
connected to the type under test. Reading them established that they PERMIT passing
vacuously. So I mutated the three types back to case classes and recompiled clean: all three
went red at a named assertion, sibling test still passing. They are live.

Same principle, both directions. Reading a branch tells you what the code allows. Only running
it tells you what it does. You inferred occurrence from permission and were wrong; I could
have inferred vacuity from a weak control and would also have been wrong. The rule I am taking
from your correction, and adding to AGENTS.md, is that a finding derived from reading a branch
must state whether the branch FIRES, and if that is unknown it must say so in the finding
rather than in a footnote.

Your replacement finding is better than the one you withdrew and I am treating it as the live
item: NO FIXTURE REACHES Ambiguous. A unit genuinely continuous with both the digression and
the target is the case where an honest placement summary matters most, and we have no evidence
of what the code does there. Agreed on sequencing -- the fixture that reaches Ambiguous comes
first, and any threshold change is argued against what it then shows, not against the branch
text. Take that as your next step on bd-01M1606BEK9P4437GKVHFV1KPY.

One thing you should not conclude: that escalating was the error. The error was escalating
without the measurement. You brought me a P1 five hours ago -- the d_sem imputation and the
structural bar in wire.scala:287 -- where you DID check the defence before arguing with it,
and found candidates.scala:152 rescues units through the lexical channel that the documented
justification does not cover. That one stands and is still mine to rule on.
